fetched.title: Use Consensus in ChatGPT, Claude, Copilot, or with the API - Consensus
fetched.text:
If you already use ChatGPT, Claude, or Microsoft 365 Copilot, connect Consensus to it. Your assistant can then search over 400 million scholarly articles, including 350 million peer-reviewed research papers, apply academic filters, hand research questions to the Consensus research agent, and cite real research instead of answering from memory.

## Connect in one click

Pick your assistant and add Consensus from its app directory.

## ChatGPT

Add Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory.

## Claude

Add Consensus from the Claude connectors directory.

## Microsoft 365 Copilot

Add Consensus for Copilot from the Microsoft Marketplace.

Sign in with your Consensus account the first time you connect. Your results depend on your Consensus plan, not your ChatGPT, Claude, or Copilot subscription.

### Connect another tool

Using a different assistant or tool, such as Cursor, VS Code, or Claude Code? Connect it to the Consensus MCP server directly. MCP (Model Context Protocol) is a standard way for AI assistants to use outside tools. The server is hosted, so there’s nothing to install:

```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

## Set up your client

Step-by-step connection guides for Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Copilot Studio, and any other MCP client.

## What your assistant can do

**Search.** The `search` tool returns ranked papers with title, authors, journal, publication year, citation count, study type, a key takeaway, and a link to the paper on Consensus. On paid plans it also returns query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers, so your assistant can quote the passage behind each claim. Your assistant can pass the same filters Research Agent uses:

* Year range, study type, and journal quartile (SJR)
* Human and controlled studies, minimum sample size, minimum citations
* Medical mode, open access only, exclude preprints
* Study duration and country

**Read whole papers.** On paid plans, `get_full_text` reads the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, so your assistant can work from a paper’s methods and results, not just its abstract.
**Threads.** With a signed-in account, your assistant can also run Research Agent as a Thread. `create_thread` starts the agent on a research question, `get_thread` returns the cited answer when it’s ready, `add_to_thread` asks a follow-up, and `find_threads` finds earlier Threads. The agent can search your Library collections and save papers to them, and `deep` mode runs a longer literature review on paid plans.

## Quick start: Search & Threads

When to use each, with a reference page for every tool.

## Supported clients

Claude (web, desktop, and Claude Code), ChatGPT and ChatGPT Deep Research, Codex, Cursor, VS Code and GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, Gemini Spark, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Copilot Studio, and any client that supports remote MCP servers.

* Claude
* ChatGPT
* Microsoft 365 Copilot

Open **Settings › Connectors**, search for Consensus, and click **+**. Then switch it on from the **+** menu in any chat under **Connectors**.

Open **Apps**, search for Consensus, and connect. It also works inside **Deep research**: open **Sources** and toggle Consensus on.

In ChatGPT Deep research, Consensus appears under Sources.

In Microsoft 365 Copilot, Consensus is a connector your admin adds for your organization. Once it’s there:

1. Select the **gear icon** at the bottom of the left sidebar, then **Settings › Sources**.
2. Find **Consensus for Copilot**, select **Connect**, and sign in with your Consensus account.
3. Ask a research question, and Copilot calls Consensus to find relevant papers.

Don’t see Consensus under **Sources**? Send your admin the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin guide.

You can use the MCP server without an account at reduced limits.

## Pre-built workflows

Consensus publishes prompt templates (“skills”) for common research jobs you can run through MCP:

* **Literature review helper** — reconnaissance, PICO/SPIDER decomposition, systematic searching, and synthesis.
* **Curriculum development** — parse a syllabus into a reading list with discussion questions.
* **Grant research** — position your idea, map it to NIH institutes and mechanisms, and find funded overlap.

See Skills, or browse the full gallery in Use cases.

## Use the API

Building your own tool, agent, or workflow? The Consensus API gives you the same paper search over REST, and can run Research Agent as a Thread. Send a query, get back ranked peer-reviewed papers with metadata, and skip running each search by hand. It’s self-serve and open to everyone.

```
GET https://api.consensus.app/v1/search
```

* The top 20 most relevant papers per query by default; raise `page_size` for more, up to your plan’s maximum
* Metadata on every paper: title, authors, journal, year, DOI, citation count, and a link
* On paid plans: study design, journal rank, key takeaways, and query-relevant excerpts from open-access papers
* The same filters as the web app: publication date, study type, sample size, citations, journal quality, field, country, and open access

To get a key, click your profile icon in Consensus, choose **API & MCP Dashboard**, open **Keys and Clients**, and click **New key**.

## Get started with the API

Authentication, your first request, and the full parameter reference.

## Run Research Agent from code

Start a Thread, wait for the cited answer, and ask follow-ups.

## Plans and limits

API and MCP calls share one monthly pool.


| Plan | Max papers per call | Included calls per month | Rate limit | Extra fields |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| No account | 3 | No monthly limit | 5 per second, shared | — |
| Free | 10 | 30 | 1 per second | — |
| Pro | 300 | 500 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI |
| Deep | 750 | 2,000 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI |
| Teams | 300 | 500 | 3 per second | Study type, takeaway, DOI |
| Enterprise | 1,000 | Custom | Custom | Study type, takeaway, DOI |

* A call covers up to 100 papers: 1–100 papers is 1 call, 101–200 is 2, and so on. Requests default to 20 papers.
* Paid plans can enable **additional usage** at $0.05 per call, up to 1,000 calls per month (10,000 on Deep). It’s off by default.
* Usage resets on the 1st of each month.

See MCP plans and access for the full breakdown.
Track usage, connected clients, and billing from your profile icon under **API & MCP Dashboard**.

Connected MCP clients appear under Keys and clients, alongside your API keys.

Clients without OAuth can pass any Consensus API key as a Bearer token. The key gets its owner’s plan limits. See MCP plans and access. For custom Enterprise limits, contact [email protected].

## Security

Only connect to the official URL above. Queries travel over HTTPS, results contain publicly available paper metadata, and no personal data is stored from MCP requests.

## Related

## Get started with MCP

Connect your client in under 2 minutes.

## API

The same search over REST.

fetched.title: Get started with Consensus MCP - Consensus
fetched.text:
One hosted server covers every field of science, so you don’t need separate PubMed, OpenAlex or Semantic Scholar servers. Your assistant gets ranked papers it can filter by study design, sample size and journal quality, and cites real studies in its answers. Connect your client below. You’ll be searching in under 2 minutes.

## What you can build with the Consensus MCP

MCP is the fastest way to give an assistant or agent paper search. Owkin plugged Consensus MCP into its agentic AI scientist and went from curated PubMed abstracts to 25x the paper coverage in days. Browse the use cases.

**Server URL**

```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

## Claude

Add Consensus from the Claude connectors directory.

## ChatGPT

Add Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory.

## Microsoft 365 Copilot

Add Consensus for Copilot from the Microsoft Marketplace.

## Perplexity

Add Consensus from the Perplexity Computer connectors store.

## How Consensus compares

In blinded evaluations on real user queries, Consensus search returns more relevant papers than Google Scholar and than frontier models with web search. See Benchmarks.

## More relevant than Google Scholar

88.1% vs 81.8% precision on 500 real user queries, judged blind by PhD researchers.

## Beats GPT-5.5 and Opus 4.8, 10x faster

More relevant top-20 papers at a median of 8.7 seconds, versus 75 to 103 seconds.

## Connect Your Client

Claude Desktop

**One-click:** open Consensus in the Claude directory and click **Connect**. Or connect manually:

1

Open Settings

Open claude.ai or the Claude desktop app and go to **Settings**.

2

Browse connectors

Select **Connectors**, then **Browse connectors**.

3

Find Consensus

Search for **Consensus** and click **Connect**.

4

Sign in

Approve the sign-in with your Consensus account, or continue without one at reduced limits.

5

Start searching

Ask a research question in any chat. Consensus appears in the tools menu.

Claude Code

```
claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

OAuth will open in your browser automatically on first use. You can also trigger it manually with the `/mcp` command inside Claude Code.

ChatGPT

**One-click:** open Consensus in the ChatGPT app directory and click **Connect**. Or connect manually:

1

Open ChatGPT

Open chatgpt.com and sign in.

2

Find Consensus

Open **Apps** from the sidebar, search for **Consensus**, and click **Connect**.

3

Sign in

Sign in with your Consensus account when prompted.

4

Start searching

Ask a research question, or call it by name: “Use Consensus to find RCTs on…”

Search results display in an interactive widget showing top papers with citations and direct links.

Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. See Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research below.

Codex

```
codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
codex mcp login consensus
```

Or add to `~/.codex/config.toml`:

```
[mcp_servers.consensus]
url = "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
```

Cursor

**One-click:** Install in Cursor. Or add to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "consensus": {
      "command": "npx",
      "args": ["-y", "mcp-remote@latest", "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"]
    }
  }
}
```

VS Code (GitHub Copilot)

Add to your MCP configuration:

```
{
  "servers": {
    "consensus": {
      "url": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Windsurf

Add to your MCP configuration:

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "consensus": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp"
    }
  }
}
```

Gemini Spark

Add Consensus as a custom app for Gemini Spark:

1

Open Connected Apps

Go to gemini.google.com and sign in with a personal Google Account, then click **Settings & help** → **Connected Apps**.

2

Add a custom app

Under **Custom apps for Spark**, click **Add a custom app** and paste the server URL:

```
https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
```

3

Approve the connection

Click **Next** and follow the prompts to finish OAuth. If your client doesn’t support Dynamic Client Registration, expand **Advanced features** and enter your credentials.

4

Start searching

Ask Gemini Spark a research question and it can call Consensus tools.

Requires access to Gemini Spark, a personal Google Account, Keep Activity turned on, and is currently available in the US. Workspace and school accounts are not supported yet.

Perplexity

1

Open the Consensus connector

2

Add the connector

Click **+ Add Connector**.

3

Sign in with Consensus

Complete the OAuth sign-in with your Consensus account. You need a Consensus account, which is free to create.

4

Confirm the connection

Click **Connect** on the OAuth confirmation screen.

5

Open Computer

Click **Computer**.

6

Ask a research question

Say “Use Consensus to…” followed by a scientific question, for example: “Use Consensus to identify the pros and cons of GLP-1s.”

Microsoft 365 Copilot

In Microsoft 365 Copilot, Consensus is a connector your admin sets up for the tenant. Once it’s there, connect it yourself under **Sources**.

1

Open Copilot Chat settings

In Microsoft 365 Copilot, select the **gear icon** at the bottom of the left sidebar, then **Settings**, then **Sources**.

2

Connect Consensus

Find **Consensus for Copilot** and select **Connect**, then sign in with your Consensus account.

3

Ask a research question

Type a research question like ‘What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?’ and Copilot will call Consensus to find relevant papers.

Don’t see Consensus under Sources? Your admin needs to add it first. Send them the Microsoft 365 Copilot admin guide. A Consensus account is required and free to create.

Microsoft 365 Copilot Studio

This allows you to add Consensus as a custom tool in Copilot studio so it can be used with agents or other automations you have have. This type of authentication will 

1

Open custom tools

Go to Copilot studio and find the ‘tools’ tab on the left hand side.

2

Create 'Create new tool'

Click ‘new tool’ to add a custom tool

3

Click 'Model context protocol'

You can also use the API to do this. But to use the MCP, click ‘model context protocol’.

4

Fill in the connector information

**Server name**Consensus**Server Description**Consensus is the go-to MCP for academic research. Search 400M+ scholarly articles, including 350M peer-reviewed papers, from PubMed, Semantic Scholar, and ArXiv — filter by study type (RCTs, meta-analyses, systematic reviews), journal quality, sample size, and more. Get structured results with citations, study takeaways, and direct links, or run pre-built workflows for literature reviews, grant research, and evidence synthesis.**Server URL**https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp**Authentication**OAuth 2.0**Type**Dynamic Discovery

5

Save and use!

Thats it! This custom tool can now be used and shared with other team members. Each team member will be able to connect to their own Consensus account when they use the tool.

A Consensus account is required. It is free to create.

API key (Bearer token)

Use an API key for clients without OAuth, headless agents, and server-side automations. Send it in the `Authorization` header on every request to `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`:

```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

Create a key from your profile icon under **API & MCP Dashboard** → **Keys and clients** → **New key**. The key gets its owner’s plan limits and draws from the same monthly pool as the API. See MCP plans and access.**JSON config** (Cursor, VS Code, and most clients that accept headers):

```
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "consensus": {
      "url": "https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp",
      "headers": {
        "Authorization": "Bearer YOUR_API_KEY"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

**Claude Code:**

```
claude mcp add --transport http consensus https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp --header "Authorization: Bearer $CONSENSUS_API_KEY"
```

An invalid or revoked key fails the search with a tool error: “Your API key is invalid or expired.” Create a new key from the **API & MCP Dashboard** and update your client config.

Keep the key server-side. Don’t paste it into prompts or commit it to a repo.

Other MCP clients

Any client that supports remote MCP servers (Streamable HTTP) works. Point it at `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`. If your client supports OAuth, authentication is handled automatically.

Pick your client for step-by-step setup.

Watch: connect Consensus and run your first search

## Using Consensus with ChatGPT Deep Research

Consensus also works with ChatGPT Deep Research. When Deep Research uses the Consensus app, it can search Consensus for relevant papers and retrieve full paper details for cited results.

1

Connect the Consensus app

Connect the Consensus app in ChatGPT using the steps above.

2

Start a Deep Research request

Start a Deep Research request in ChatGPT.

3

Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus

Ask ChatGPT to use Consensus for peer-reviewed research, for example:
> Use Consensus to research the evidence on exercise for depression. Prioritize systematic reviews, meta-analyses, and randomized controlled trials.

Deep Research may run multiple Consensus searches, refine filters, retrieve paper details, and return a cited synthesis with direct links to papers on Consensus.

## Verify Your Connection

Try one of these in your connected client. Each link opens the question pre-filled:


| Ask | Try it |
| --- | --- |
| ”What does the research say about creatine and cognitive function?” | Claude · ChatGPT |
| ”Find meta-analyses on mindfulness for anxiety published since 2020” | Claude · ChatGPT |
| ”Are there RCTs on intermittent fasting with more than 500 participants?” | Claude · ChatGPT |
| ”What is the strongest evidence for and against remote work productivity?” | Claude · ChatGPT |

You should see results citing specific papers with titles, journals, years, citation counts, and direct links.

## Plans and Access

Your Consensus plan, not your AI subscription, sets how many papers each search returns, your monthly calls, whether results include DOIs and full-text excerpts, and whether Threads can use `deep` mode. No account is needed to try it.

## Plans and access

Limits for every plan, how calls are counted, additional usage, and API key access.

## Tools

Consensus MCP exposes six tools. Your assistant picks the right one from your question.


| Tool | What it does |
| --- | --- |
| `search` | Find ranked, peer-reviewed papers for a query in one call. |
| `get_full_text` | Read the complete text of open-access papers from search results or Threads, as Markdown. |
| `create_thread` | Start a Thread: hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. |
| `get_thread` | Poll a Thread and read the agent’s cited answer. |
| `add_to_thread` | Ask a follow-up in an existing Thread. |
| `find_threads` | List your Threads and find an earlier one. |

`search` works without an account. The thread tools need a signed-in Consensus account or an API key. `get_full_text` needs a paid plan.

## Quick start: Search & Threads

When to use search, when to start a Thread, and how a Thread runs.

## Troubleshooting

OAuth login is only supported for streamable HTTP servers (Codex)

You added the server with `-- --transport http` instead of `--url`. Remove and re-add:

```
codex mcp remove consensus
codex mcp add consensus --url https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp
codex mcp login consensus
```

Authentication successful but server reconnection failed (Claude Code)

Fully quit and restart Claude Code. Do not just use the reconnect option. Your credentials are saved and will work after restart.

Tools stop working after a few hours (401 errors)

Your OAuth token has expired. Re-authenticate:

* **Claude Code:** Type `/mcp`, select Consensus, choose Clear authentication, re-authenticate, then restart Claude Code
* **Codex:** Run `codex mcp logout consensus` then `codex mcp login consensus`
* **Cursor:** Disconnect and reconnect the server in Settings then Tools and MCP
* **Claude Desktop:** Disconnect and reconnect the connector in Settings then Connectors
* **ChatGPT:** Disconnect and reconnect the Consensus app from ChatGPT Apps
* **Perplexity:** Disconnect and reconnect Consensus in Computer then Connectors

Server shows failed or no tools appear

* Verify the URL includes `/mcp` at the end
* Remove and re-add the server using the commands above
* Restart your client completely

Consensus search has not been loaded yet (Claude Code)

This is normal. Claude loads tool definitions on demand when many tools are present. Retry the query and it will work on the second attempt.

ChatGPT Deep Research is not using Consensus

Confirm the Consensus app is connected in ChatGPT Apps, then ask Deep Research to use Consensus explicitly. For example:
> Use Consensus to find peer-reviewed papers on this question and cite the strongest evidence.

Deep Research decides when to call connected tools, so it may not call Consensus for questions that are not research-focused.

No results found

Try broadening your search query or removing filters. Use specific academic terminology rather than casual language.

Monthly call limit reached

Paid plans can continue making calls past the included monthly limit when the account has an active metered API subscription and additional usage is enabled; extra usage is billed at $0.05 per call, with each call covering up to 100 papers. Free plans must wait for the next monthly reset or upgrade.

Rate limit exceeded (429 error)

Rate limits are per user for authenticated MCP clients. A 429 that says you’re sending requests too quickly is a per-minute rate limit; wait a few moments and add backoff between requests. A 429 that mentions monthly call credits is a usage limit, not a rate limit.

## Security

* **Endpoint:** Only connect to the official URL: `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`
* **API keys:** Store securely using environment variables. Never share keys in prompts or public conversations. Rotate if compromised.
* **Data handling:** Search queries are sent to the Consensus API over HTTPS/TLS. Results contain publicly available academic paper metadata. No personal data is stored from MCP requests.

## Supported Platforms

| Platform | Auth | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Claude Desktop | OAuth | Supported |
| ChatGPT | OAuth | Supported |
| ChatGPT Deep Research | OAuth | Supported |
| Claude Code | OAuth | Supported |
| Codex | OAuth | Supported |
| Cursor | OAuth | Supported |
| VS Code (GitHub Copilot) | Config | Supported |
| Windsurf | Config | Supported |
| Gemini Spark | OAuth | Supported |
| Perplexity | OAuth | Supported |
| Other MCP Clients | Bearer token | Supported |

## FAQ

Is there a PubMed MCP server with semantic search?

Yes. Consensus covers all of PubMed plus the rest of science, ranked semantically rather than by keyword match alone. You can filter by study design, sample size, journal quartile and citation count. See Where the papers come from.

What's the best MCP server for scientific literature in Claude?

Consensus is in the Claude connectors directory and works in Claude on the web, the Claude desktop app and Claude Code.

How do I add a scientific search connector to ChatGPT?

Connect Consensus from the ChatGPT app directory. It also works with ChatGPT Deep Research.

Can I use a research paper search MCP server in Cursor or VS Code?

Yes. Install it in one click in Cursor, or add the server URL to your MCP configuration in VS Code (GitHub Copilot).

Which MCP server works for pharma and drug discovery?

Consensus is SOC 2 Type II compliant, doesn’t use customer data to train AI models, and offers a zero-data-retention option on enterprise agreements. It runs behind AI gateways and in Microsoft 365 Copilot. Owkin uses it in its agentic AI scientist. See Security and data handling.

Does it work for systematic reviews and meta-analyses?

Yes. Filter by study design, including RCTs, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and run deep literature reviews with Threads. See the Threads quick start.

Is this the same as Consensus (goconsensus.com)?

No. This is Consensus, the AI academic search engine at consensus.app. It’s unrelated to the sales demo platform at goconsensus.com.

## Additional Resources

## Consensus Website

Explore the Consensus research platform.

## API Documentation

Structured JSON results for pipelines and integrations.

## MCP Specification

Learn more about the Model Context Protocol.

## MCP server on GitHub

View the source, report issues, and star the Consensus MCP server.

fetched.title: Security and data handling - Consensus
fetched.text:
Consensus is a multi-tenant SaaS application: a web app, an MCP server, and a REST API, all hosted on Google Cloud Platform and reached over HTTPS. Nothing is installed on your premises and no VPN is required. This page summarizes the controls; the full picture is available under NDA for your vendor review.

## Compliance

Consensus is **SOC 2 Type II** compliant. The audit covers the security, availability, and confidentiality of the Consensus service. Request the current report and bridge letter through sales; we share it under NDA as part of your vendor review.
The hosting platform, Google Cloud, holds its own certifications, including ISO 27001, SOC 1/2/3, and PCI DSS.

## What is sent

A search request carries the user’s query and any filters (year range, study type, journal quartile, and so on), plus a credential. Requests travel over HTTPS:

* **MCP server** (`https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`): an API key or a per-user OAuth token, sent as `Authorization: Bearer`.
* **REST API** (`https://api.consensus.app/v1/search`): an API key, sent in the `x-api-key` header.

When your users upload documents or search their Library in the Consensus web app, that content stays in their private Library. The MCP server and API never read a user’s Library; they search only the public research index.

## What comes back

Publicly available academic paper metadata: title, authors, journal, year, citation count, DOI, abstract, and on paid plans a study-type classification, a key takeaway, and, for open-access papers, query-relevant excerpts from the paper’s full text. Nothing in a response is derived from your organization’s data.

## What Consensus stores

* No personal data is stored from MCP requests.
* Customer data is not used to train AI models, and the LLM providers Consensus uses retain no data from requests.
* Consensus does not share user data with third parties.
* Uploads to a user’s Library are private to that account unless the user shares a Collection.
* Enterprise agreements can include a zero-data-retention option.

## Encryption

Data is encrypted in transit with TLS 1.2 or later and at rest with AES-256. Secrets and credentials are managed in Google Cloud Secret Manager.

## Infrastructure

The service runs in a private Google Cloud VPC with restrictive firewall rules, across multiple zones with automated failover. Public traffic passes through Google Cloud Load Balancing and Cloud Armor, which provides WAF, OWASP protections, and DDoS mitigation. Internal traffic is segmented and TLS-encrypted. Enterprise agreements can include a contractual uptime SLA.

## Access control

* Customers are logically segregated within the multi-tenant environment.
* Production access is limited to authorized engineering and operations staff, requires SSO with MFA, follows least privilege, and is logged. Access grants, changes, and offboarding follow documented approval and review processes evidenced under SOC 2.
* Employee devices are managed with MDM-enforced anti-malware and full-disk encryption.

## Authentication for your users

* **SAML 2.0 single sign-on** with AD FS, Microsoft Entra ID, Okta, and other identity providers. Group-based access can be driven by SAML attribute mapping from your directory. See Single sign-on.
* **Federated authentication** for academic institutions.
* Institutional admins manage their own users and roles.
* For MCP access, users authenticate with OAuth 2.0 (authorization code with PKCE), or your gateway holds an API key server-side and sends it as a Bearer token. See the connection reference.
* For REST API access, your service sends an API key in the `x-api-key` header. The REST API doesn’t accept OAuth tokens or Bearer credentials. See API authentication.

To set up SSO or SCIM provisioning for your organization, see Single sign-on.

## Monitoring and audit logging

Access, admin, and system events are centralized in Google Cloud Logging with audit logging enabled. User sign-in and sign-out events and user actions are recorded with user attribution. Application and infrastructure monitoring runs in Datadog. Customer-specific log excerpts are available on request where contractually agreed.

## Vulnerability management

CI/CD pipelines include automated dependency and misconfiguration scanning. A third-party penetration test is performed annually, and findings are triaged by severity under the vulnerability management policy. A summary is available under NDA.

## Credentials

* **API keys** are shown once at creation, can be named, revoked, and rotated from the **API & MCP Dashboard**, and are scoped to search. Store them in your gateway’s secret store, never in client-side code.
* **OAuth tokens** are issued per user after an authorization-code flow with PKCE (S256). There is no client-credentials grant and no way to obtain a token without a user’s consent. Users can disconnect at any time from their Consensus account.

## Endpoint integrity

Only connect to the official endpoint, `https://mcp.consensus.app/mcp`. The OAuth discovery documents at `mcp.consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource` and `consensus.app/.well-known/oauth-authorization-server` let a gateway verify the authorization server it is talking to.

## Contracts and data lifecycle

Consensus can execute a mutual NDA and a data-processing agreement. Contracts can include terms for the return and irrecoverable disposal of your data at termination.

## Reviews and questionnaires

For the SOC 2 Type II report, penetration-test summary, network topology, security questionnaires, DPAs, or SSO setup, contact sales.

fetched.title: Quick start: Threads - Consensus
fetched.text:
The Threads endpoints hand a research question to the Consensus research agent. The agent searches the literature, reads the papers, and writes a markdown answer with citations. You create a Thread, poll it until the answer is ready, and add follow-ups that keep the earlier context.

## Search vs Threads

Search returns papers and leaves the reasoning to your code. A Thread hands the whole research task to an agent, which runs many steps and writes the answer for you.


|  | Search | Threads |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **You get back** | A list of papers with abstracts and metadata | A list of papers, a written analysis, a reasoning trace (with `include_trace=true`), and citations with grounding quotes |
| **Functionality** | Semantic paper search with filters | Search, citation crawls, author search, finding specific papers, reading full papers, searching attached collections, and reading and writing your Library collections |
| **Steps per request** | One | Many |
| **Timing** | Synchronous | Asynchronous |
| **Follow-ups** | Each request stands alone | Ask follow-up questions that build on earlier answers |

Need the raw papers for your own pipeline, or a quick lookup? Use Search.

## What you can ask a Thread

Each of these needs several research steps in one request, which Search can’t do. Click a card for the request body.

## Crawl citations

Trace what a paper built on and the work that followed it.

## Read specific papers

Compare the methods and findings of papers you choose.

## Research an author

Summarize an author’s work on a topic and how it changed.

## Run deep research

Get a structured literature review built from about 50 papers.

## Build on an earlier answer

Narrow or extend the last answer without starting over.

## How it works

Threads are asynchronous. A `pro` run usually finishes in under a minute, and a `deep` run takes a few minutes.

1

Create a Thread

`POST /v1/threads` starts the run and returns a `thread_id` right away, with `status: "running"`.

2

Poll until it's done

`GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}` until `status` is `idle` (answer ready) or `failed`. Wait `poll_after_seconds` between polls: 5 seconds for `pro`, 20 for `deep`.

3

Ask a follow-up

`POST /v1/threads/{thread_id}/interactions` continues the Thread. Poll again for the new answer.

## Create a Thread

Send the complete research brief in `input_message`. The agent doesn’t ask clarifying questions, so include the whole task in one message.

```
curl -X POST "https://api.consensus.app/v1/threads" \
  -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{
    "input_message": "What dose of creatine improves working memory in healthy adults, and how strong is the evidence?",
    "mode": "pro",
    "filters": { "year_min": 2010, "human": true }
  }'
```

```
{
  "thread_id": "<thread_id>",
  "interaction_id": "<interaction_id>",
  "title": "Creatine dose and working memory in healthy adults",
  "status": "running",
  "mode": "pro",
  "url": "https://consensus.app/search/creatine-dose-and-working-memory-in-healthy-adults/<thread_id>/",
  "poll_after_seconds": 5,
  "max_wait_seconds": 180
}
```

* **`mode`:** controls how much effort the agent spends. `pro` (the default) fits most questions. `deep` reads more papers and writes a longer, structured report.
* **`filters`:** the same filters as `GET /v1/search`, such as `year_min`, `study_types`, `human`, and `sjr_max`. They apply to every search the agent runs.
* **`attachments`:** focus the research on up to 50 `paper_ids` or 10 Library `collection_ids`. A collection’s id is the number in its web URL, `consensus.app/library/{id}/`.
* **`skill`:** run a named research workflow, a Skill, instead of the agent’s open-ended plan: `literature-review`, `citation-snowballing`, `find-citations`, or `verify-citations`. It requires `mode` set to `deep`. Leave it unset for normal research.

## Poll for the answer

```
curl "https://api.consensus.app/v1/threads/<thread_id>" -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY"
```

While the run is going, `status` is `running`. When it’s `idle`, the latest interaction carries the answer:

```
{
  "thread_id": "<thread_id>",
  "title": "Creatine dose and working memory in healthy adults",
  "status": "idle",
  "url": "https://consensus.app/search/creatine-dose-and-working-memory-in-healthy-adults/<thread_id>/",
  "interactions": [
    {
      "interaction_id": "<interaction_id>",
      "status": "idle",
      "mode": "pro",
      "response": "Short-term loading at about 20 g/day improved working memory in some trials [1.1] …",
      "citations": [
        {
          "n": 1,
          "paper_id": "<paper_id>",
          "title": "Creatine and improvement in cognitive function: Evaluation of a health claim …",
          "year": 2024,
          "journal": "EFSA Journal",
          "url": "https://consensus.app/papers/…",
          "snippets": [
            { "marker": "1.1", "quote": "…", "section": "Weighing of the evidence" }
          ]
        }
      ],
      "stats": { "retrieved": 120, "screened": 40, "included": 18 }
    }
  ]
}
```

Illustrative and trimmed. In `response`, a marker like `[1.1]` cites quote 1 from paper 1, and a bare `[1]` cites the paper without a quote. Each `citations[].snippets[].marker` matches a marker in the text. Quotes can come from the full text of any paper the analysis cites, paywalled papers from Consensus’s publisher partners included.

* **How long to wait:** stop polling after `max_wait_seconds`, about 3 minutes for `pro` and 10 minutes for `deep`.
* **Agent steps:** add `include_trace=true` to get `agent_trace`, a plain-English list of the steps the agent took. It’s written for display, so don’t parse it.
* **Skill:** an interaction that ran a Skill carries `skill`, such as `literature-review` or `verify-citations`: the one requested, otherwise the one the agent chose itself. It’s omitted when none applies.
* **Earlier turns:** only the latest interaction carries `response` and `citations`. Pass `interaction_id` to read an earlier one.
* **Institutional full-text links:** on a paid plan, if you’ve selected your institution in Consensus settings, citations can include an `institutional_access_url` that opens the full text through your library. Only the first 50 distinct DOIs are looked up.

## Ask a follow-up

```
curl -X POST "https://api.consensus.app/v1/threads/<thread_id>/interactions" \
  -H "x-api-key: $CONSENSUS_API_KEY" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{ "input_message": "Do the results differ for adults over 60?" }'
```

The agent already has the earlier turns, so don’t restate them. A follow-up sent while the latest interaction is still `running` returns `409`. Wait until the Thread is `idle` or `failed`, then send it.
To find earlier Threads, `GET /v1/threads` lists yours newest first. Pass `query` to match on title.

## Work in your Library

With a personal API key, the agent can read and write your Library as part of a Thread. Ask in plain language in `input_message`, and name collections the way they appear in Consensus. If two collections share a name, also name the parent collection, for example “the Methods collection inside Sleep”. There are no separate Library endpoints.


| Action | Example `input_message` |
| --- | --- |
| List your collections, with their paper counts and your role on each | ”List all of my Library collections and how many papers each has.” |
| List the papers in a collection, filtered by publication year, date added, or a title, author, or journal match | ”Which papers in my Sleep collection were published before 2020?” |
| Search within your collections | ”What do the papers in my Sleep collection say about magnesium?” |
| Create a collection, at the top level or inside another one | ”Create a collection called Magnesium inside my Sleep collection.” |
| Save papers the agent found into a collection | ”Find 10 RCTs on magnesium and sleep quality and save them to my Sleep collection.” |
| Rename a collection | ”Rename my Sleep collection to Sleep and Supplements.” |

* **Saves don’t pause for confirmation.** The agent saves papers as soon as you ask, and the answer says how many it added and how many were already there.
* **No surprise collections.** The agent creates a collection only when you ask for one. If you name a collection that doesn’t exist, it reports it as not found instead of creating it.
* **Removing, deleting, and moving are web-only.** These need a confirmation step, so they’re available only in the Consensus web app. Over the API, the agent tells you to make the change there.
* **Listings stop at 100 collections.** In a larger Library, the rest are summarized as “and N more”, and you can’t page through them.
* **Personal keys only.** An organization API key has no Library, so its Threads can’t list or change collections.

The Thread’s `response` reports what changed.

## Example requests

Each example shows the request body. Send it the same way as in Create a Thread, then poll for the answer.

### Crawl citations from a seed paper

The agent follows the citation graph backward and forward from a paper you name.

```
{
  "input_message": "Start from Cong et al. 2013, the first report of CRISPR-Cas9 genome editing in mammalian cells. Trace the earlier work it built on and the most-cited papers that followed it, and summarize how the method evolved."
}
```

### Read and compare specific papers

Attach papers with `attachments.paper_ids`, and the agent reads them before it answers. Paper IDs come from `citations[].paper_id` in an earlier Thread.

```
{
  "input_message": "Compare the methods, sample sizes, and effect sizes across these papers, and explain where their conclusions disagree.",
  "attachments": { "paper_ids": ["<paper_id_1>", "<paper_id_2>", "<paper_id_3>"] }
}
```

### Research an author

The agent looks up papers by a named author, then synthesizes them.

```
{
  "input_message": "Summarize Walter Willett's research on dietary fat and heart disease, and how his conclusions changed over time."
}
```

### Run a deep literature review

Set `mode` to `deep` for a structured report built from about 50 papers. A `deep` run takes up to about 10 minutes and requires a paid plan.

```
{
  "input_message": "Write a literature review on GLP-1 receptor agonists and cardiovascular outcomes. Cover mechanisms, the major trials, safety signals, and open questions.",
  "mode": "deep",
  "filters": { "year_min": 2015 }
}
```

### Run a skill

Set `skill` to run a named workflow, on a new Thread or a follow-up. Skills run in `deep` mode, so set `mode` to `deep` too. `find-citations` and `verify-citations` work on a draft, so put the draft text in `input_message`.

```
{
  "input_message": "Check whether the citations in this paragraph support its claims: …",
  "mode": "deep",
  "skill": "verify-citations"
}
```

A request with `skill` is refused with `422` if `mode` isn’t `deep`, if you use an organization API key, or if the skill needs input the request didn’t include. If skills aren’t enabled for your account yet, it returns `403` `feature_not_allowed`.

### Save papers to a collection

The agent runs the research, then saves the papers it found into a collection you name. Ask for a new collection explicitly if you want one.

```
{
  "input_message": "Find 10 randomized controlled trials on magnesium supplementation and sleep quality in adults, summarize their findings, and save them to a new collection called Magnesium and Sleep."
}
```

### Audit and tidy a collection

The agent lists a collection’s papers with filters, reads them, and renames the collection.

```
{
  "input_message": "List the papers in my Sleep collection published before 2015, summarize which of their conclusions newer work has overturned, then rename the collection to Sleep - foundational."
}
```

### Build on an earlier answer

Send a follow-up to `POST /v1/threads/{thread_id}/interactions`. The agent reads the earlier turns, so you can refer to them directly.

```
{
  "input_message": "Of the trials you cited, keep only the randomized controlled trials with more than 100 participants. Does the conclusion change?"
}
```

## Good to know

* **Cost:** a Thread draws from the same monthly calls as search, and it’s charged by the amount of work the agent does. `mode` controls the effort, so a `deep` run costs more than a `pro` run. A failed run costs nothing. See plans and access.
* **Rate limits:** one request per second, except polling a Thread, which allows three per second.
* **Don’t retry blindly on `5xx`.** The Thread or follow-up may already have been created. List your Threads or poll the Thread before you send it again.

## Endpoint reference

## Start a Thread

`POST /v1/threads`

## Poll a Thread

`GET /v1/threads/{thread_id}`

## Add a follow-up

`POST /v1/threads/{thread_id}/interactions`

## List historical Threads

`GET /v1/threads`
